about.what: Qualitative photo cases. Real meal photographs, labelled by eye.
about.why_not_weighed: These have no weighed ground truth, so they cannot measure calorie accuracy — a person estimating portions from an image averages ~41% error (Nutrition5k), which is larger than the thing we would be trying to measure. They are scored on what CAN be judged from a photograph: did it name the right foods, did it admit the ones it does not know, and did it invent anything.

scoring.identified: foods the system named correctly, by our own database's vocabulary
scoring.admitted: foods it correctly declined to guess at (not in the database)
scoring.invented: foods reported that are not in the picture — must be 0
scoring.invisible: calories no photograph can show: oil, sauce, dressing, sugar. Recorded per case so the systematic undercount is visible rather than silently absorbed.

cases.describe: Bowl of soy-glazed ramen noodles, spring onion and sesame seeds on top, chopsticks lifting a strand.
cases.invisible: The glaze is soy, sugar and sesame oil. A tablespoon of sesame oil alone is ~120 kcal and nothing in the frame shows it.
cases.probes: A single-food bowl where the food is easy and the sauce carrying much of the energy is undetectable. Also tests whether a near-miss (pasta for ramen) is reported honestly or dressed up as a match.

cases.describe: Plate of flour-coated fried anchovies (hamsi tava) with lemon wedges, parsley and sliced red onion.
cases.invisible: Deep-fried in oil. The coating absorbs a large and unknowable fraction.
cases.probes: Almost nothing here is in a 68-row database. The correct behaviour is to say so, not to reach for the nearest fish-shaped row. This is the ignorance test.

cases.describe: Bowl with sliced blackened chicken breast, dressed romaine, sweet potato fries, lemon slice; a glass of iced cola beside it.
cases.invisible: The dressing. Creamy dressing on that much lettuce is 100-200 kcal and reads visually as almost nothing.
cases.probes: Multi-item, and the two highest-energy components (fries, dressing) are the two least likely to be handled. Tests whether a partial answer is presented as partial.

cases.describe: Pan of jumbo pasta shells stuffed with spinach and ricotta, in tomato sauce, topped with grated cheese.
cases.invisible: Nothing hidden by cooking here, but the filling is most of the energy and it is a composite the database has no template for.
cases.probes: A dish that is one thing to a person and five rows to a database. Tests composite handling, and whether the pan is read as a serving.

cases.describe: Plate with sliced medium-rare steak under chimichurri, roasted carrot sticks, steamed broccoli.
cases.invisible: Chimichurri is mostly oil. Two spoonfuls is ~200 kcal sitting in plain sight and looking like herbs.
cases.probes: The clearest case of energy hiding as garnish. Also tests whether ground beef is offered for steak, and whether that substitution is disclosed.
cases.labelNote: Labelled as sweet potato fries on first pass; the model read them as roasted carrot sticks and was right. Recorded because a labeller being wrong about a photograph is the reason these cases are not scored on calories.
